title: Real Madrid’s Rodrygo played with partial ACL tear since 2023
content:
Rodrygo carried on playing regularly for Real Madrid and Brazil despite suffering a partial anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear in his right knee when on international duty in 2023.

On Tuesday, the 25-year-old was diagnosed with a rupture of the ACL and the lateral meniscus of that knee, an injury suffered in Monday’s 1-0 home defeat by Getafe in La Liga.

It is expected Rodrygo will be out for up to a year, which means he will miss the World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico this summer.

After a thorough examination by doctors back in 2023, the decision was made for the Madrid forward not to have surgery on his partial ACL tear when he was back in the Spanish capital, and he continued to be available for selection.

Sources with knowledge of the situation, speaking anonymously as they were not authorised to comment, said a more conservative course of treatment was considered appropriate because a partial ACL tear does not always require surgery.

They said that while it was true there might be a risk of suffering a more serious problem to the ACL, that risk could be sensibly mitigated by greater “preventative work”, such as physiotherapy and gym sessions.

Sources said the process followed was correct and that there have been other similar cases in football. This was also reflected in messages from Rodrygo’s closest representatives to The Athletic, when consulted for this article.

The Brazilian’s spokesperson, Fernando Torres, said: “All his physical issues have always received the most appropriate solutions for the best recovery and sequence.

“The priority now is the treatment of this injury and the pooling of efforts and energies for the player’s return to the field.

On Monday, Rodrygo was making his first Madrid appearance since February 1, as he had been suffering from tendinosis in his right hamstring.

In an Instagram post on Tuesday, Rodrygo wrote: “One of the worst days of my life, how much I always feared this injury … maybe life has been a little cruel to me lately. I don’t know if I deserve this, but what can I complain about? How many wonderful things I’ve already experienced, which I also didn’t deserve.”

Rodrygo is the fifth Madrid player to sustain an ACL injury since the summer of 2023, joining a list that also features goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois, David Alaba, and Dani Carvajal. His compatriot Eder Militao has sustained the injury twice in recent seasons, in August 2023 and then in November 2024.
